desc:
Count the orderings p of the numbers 1..n in which no two neighbouring entries are consecutive integers: |p[i] - p[i+1]| != 1 for every index i.

Return the count modulo 1,000,000,007.

n = 4  ->  2     ([2,4,1,3] and [3,1,4,2])
n = 5  ->  14
n = 3  ->  0
n = 1  ->  1
hints: Brute force over all n! orderings only works for n up to about 10. Instead of forbidding bad neighbours, count the orderings in which chosen neighbour pairs are bad, and use inclusion-exclusion.

Pick a set S of k of the n-1 value pairs (v, v+1) and force each of them to be adjacent. Chains of chosen pairs glue into blocks. A block of two or more values can appear ascending or descending, and the n - k blocks and loose values can be ordered in (n - k)! ways.

If the k chosen pairs form m runs of consecutive pairs, the count for S is (n-k)! * 2^m. The number of ways to choose k pairs forming m runs is C(k-1, m-1) * C(n-k, m). Sum with alternating signs over k.
editorial: Inclusion-exclusion on the n - 1 “bad” pairs {v, v+1}. For a set S of k pairs, the orderings in which every pair of S is adjacent are obtained by gluing: a maximal run of j chosen pairs ties j + 1 values into one block whose inner order is forced up to reversal (2 ways), so S yields (n - k)! · 2<sup>m</sup> orderings where m is the number of runs and n - k is the number of resulting items.

Choosing k of the n - 1 pairs so that they form exactly m runs: split k into m positive parts, C(k-1, m-1) ways, and place the m runs among the n - 1 - k unchosen pairs, C(n-k, m) ways. Therefore the answer is n! + sum over k = 1..n-1 of (-1)^k (n-k)! sum over m of C(k-1, m-1) C(n-k, m) 2^m, taken modulo p. With factorial tables and inverse factorials this is O(n2) (about n2/4 terms).
The values 1, 0, 0, 2, 14, 90, 646, 5242 for n = 1..8 are a handy check (known as Hertzsprung's problem). A bitmask DP over (used set, last value) also works but only up to n of about 16.
solution:
def countNoConsecutive(n):
    M = 1000000007
    fact = [1] * (n + 2)
    for i in range(1, n + 2):
        fact[i] = fact[i - 1] * i % M
    ifact = [pow(f, M - 2, M) for f in fact]
    pw = [1] * (n + 2)
    for i in range(1, n + 2):
        pw[i] = pw[i - 1] * 2 % M
    total = fact[n]
    for k in range(1, n):
        s = 0
        for m in range(1, min(k, n - k) + 1):
            s += ifact[m - 1] * ifact[k - m] % M * ifact[m] % M * ifact[n - k - m] % M * pw[m]
        s %= M
        s = s * fact[k - 1] % M * fact[n - k] % M * fact[n - k] % M
        total += -s if k & 1 else s
    return total % M
